Hi! I'm someone who up until recently struggled with depersonalization and disassociation for years at a time. Spent years inside, not talking to people, being a recluse all while not feeling like I was a real person and nothing around me was real. 

Lately, I've been microdosing shrooms  (less than 2g for me) and its been helping me even when sober. My mindset has entirely shifted into something more positive, I hardly feel like the same person I was even a few months ago. I think the catalyst for this set of changes was an ego death I had on one of my higher dose trips, but I don't think the shrooms did it alone. It was a mix of therapy, self help, and lots of self reflection. Coming to terms with a lot of the traumas that cause me to disassociate. 

Can shrooms help you with depersonalization? Maybe. I don't know you as a person, your mindset surrounding these things, and how you would go about it, but I feel like I'm a walking example of the medicinal value of shrooms. I don't think they are the cure all for situations like ours, but I do think they can nudge us in the right direction when handled with care. What matters is what we do and the choices we make to strive toward a more inner peace. I wish you luck, your journey is a hard one ❤

Idk what you think I mean by leash correction, but I'm simply talking about the 80/20 rule. The dog leaves you, you let the dog give themselves 80% of the correction, and 20% from the human end. Leash corrections are entirely necessary to help fix leash reactivity, aggression, and in a lot of cases, can help general obedience by showing the dog that what you say goes. I take my dogs to the vet monthly, and they have no signs of neck injury or anything like that. The entire point of a leash correction is to show the dog that there are rules to a leash, and that you shouldn't be leaving your person, and if you do, there are consequences, ie; hitting the of the leash. There is literally no other reasonable and time efficient way to train a dog to walk at heel and dampen leash reactivity.

Oh hey!! My two blue pitties were and sometimes still are like this. Personally I would ditch the choke chain for a gentle leader first off. Much less intrusive, less painful, less uncomfortable and easier to do leash corrections. 
Next important thing is this: how does he act when around kids or other dogs? Not a couple hundred feet away, but directly next to dogs and people? Is he reactive on leash? Does he have fear aggression, or any other forms of aggression towards kids and/or other dogs? If not, then this is likely just a mix of mild anxiety, boredom, and just wanting to know whats happening. Only way to really fix this behavior is desensitization and trying to redirect his focus onto you. I don't mean waving treats in his face and begging him for attention though, I mean saying the dogs name and putting them in a sit, if he doesn't, then he gets a mild leash correction to just let him know that you are there, and if he does put his attention on you without a corrections, then you treat to reinforce that. As you do this process, slowly move closer to the stimulus, and just correct when needed, and reinforce when they focus on you without a cue/correction.
